simple.meaning: אָלַח (ʼâlach) is a Hebrew word meaning “to muddle , i.e. (figuratively and intransitive) to turn (morally) corrupt.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אָלַח (H444) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Job 15:16, with occurrences in Job, Psalms.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָלַח (H444) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אָלַח (H444) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אָלַח (ʼâlach) / H444 is traced through Job 15:16, Psalms 14:3, Psalms 53:4 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H444. alach [ אָלַח ] verb only Niph`al be corrupt morally ; tainted (Che Psa 14:3 ) (compare Arabic VIII. be confused (of a thing), of milk, turn sour ) Perfect 3plural נֶאֱלָ֑חוּ 14:3 ; 53:4 ; Participle נֶאֱלָח a corrupt man Job 15:16 .
